subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: x−3y−5=0 is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the points A and B. Given A=(−1,−3), find the coordinates of B.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 41, book p.148. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split gives one mark for writing BOTH bisector conditions as two equations in h and k, and one for solving them. B = (−8/5, −6/5) was obtained twice by independent routes — the two-condition route written on the page, and the reflection formula (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = −2(ax₁ + by₁ + c)/(a² + b²) — and then checked: the midpoint (−13/10, −21/10) satisfies x − 3y − 5 = 0, and the slope of AB is −3, so (1/3)(−3) = −1. The fractional answer is correct, not a slip. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say the two things a perpendicular bisector tells you, and how many unknowns you are solving for.

steps.label: Write both bisector conditions
steps.margin_note: First mark. A perpendicular bisector gives TWO facts, not one: the midpoint is on the line, and the segment is perpendicular to it. Two unknowns need two equations.
steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular bisector = midpoint on the line AND segment perpendicular to it. Two conditions, two unknowns.
lines: (i) the midpoint of AB lies on the line,
(ii) AB is perpendicular to the line.
(the midpoint formula, with A(−1, −3) and B(h, k))

lines.text: so the slope of AB is −3)

recall.must_convey: That both conditions are written: the midpoint of AB lies on the line, and AB is perpendicular to it.

steps.why: Either condition alone gives only one equation in h and k, so it cannot fix B. The midpoint condition alone leaves B anywhere on h − 3k − 2 = 0, and perpendicularity alone leaves B anywhere on 3h + k + 6 = 0; only both together fix B.
common_mistakes: Using only the midpoint condition, which leaves B undetermined.
Taking the slope of AB as 1/3, the slope of the line itself.

steps.label: Solve for B
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two linear equations in h and k. Substituting (2) into (1) is quickest, and the answer is a pair of fractions.
steps.memory_tip: Make one unknown the subject in the simpler equation, substitute into the other, then go back for it.

recall.must_convey: That solving the two equations gives B = (−8/5, −6/5).

steps.why: B is the reflection of A in the given line, so the same answer also comes from the reflection formula; solving the two conditions is the version that needs no formula to be remembered.
common_mistakes: Sign slip when moving the constant across, writing 10h = 16 instead of 10h = −16.
Solving for h and stopping there, without also solving for k.
